actions.notion_add_comment.description: Posts a new comment thread on a Notion page.
actions.notion_add_comment.props.comment: The plain-text comment to post as a new thread on the page.
actions.notion_add_comment.props.page_id: The id of the page to comment on. Resolve via notion_search.
actions.notion_append_to_page.descriptio: Appends new block content (parsed from markdown) to the end of a page or block.
actions.notion_append_to_page.props.bloc: The id of the page or block to append content to. Resolve via notion_search (page) or notion_get_block_children (block).
actions.notion_append_to_page.props.cont: The content to append. Markdown formatting is supported. Each resulting text block is capped at 2000 characters by Notion.
actions.notion_archive_database_item.des: Archives (soft-deletes) a Notion database item by its page id, keeping it recoverable.
actions.notion_archive_database_item.pro: The page id of the database row to archive. Resolve it via notion_query_database or notion_find_database_item.
actions.notion_archive_page.description: Archives (trashes) or restores any page or database row by id via its archived flag.
actions.notion_archive_page.props.archiv: Set to true to archive (trash) the page, false to restore it.
actions.notion_archive_page.props.page_i: The id of the page (or database row) to archive or restore. Resolve via notion_search.
actions.notion_create_database.descripti: Creates a new inline Notion database under a parent page, with a title and a property-schema object defining its columns.
actions.notion_create_database.props.par: The id of the PAGE the new database will live under (must be a page, not a database). Resolve it via notion_search.
actions.notion_create_database.props.pro: A Notion property-schema object: a map of column name to a type-config object. Example: { "Name": { "title": {} }, "Status": { "select": { "options": [ { "name": "Open" }, { "name": "Done" } ] } }, "Estimate": { "number": { "format": "number" } } }. EXACTLY ONE property must be of type "title". Common types: title:{}, rich_text:{}, number:{format}, select:{options:[{name,color?}]}, multi_select:{options:[...]}, date:{}, checkbox:{}, url:{}, email:{}, phone_number:{}, people:{}, relation:{database_id}.
actions.notion_create_database.props.tit: The title of the new database.
actions.notion_create_database_item.desc: Creates a new row (page) in a Notion database, setting its property values from a raw Notion properties object, with optional body content.
actions.notion_create_database_item.prop: Optional plain-text paragraph to append as the body of the new row (page).
The id of the database to add a row to. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).

A Notion properties object: a map of property name to a typed value object matching the database schema. Example: { "Name": { "title": [ { "text": { "content": "My task" } } ] }, "Status": { "status": { "name": "In Progress" } }, "Estimate": { "number": 3 }, "Tags": { "multi_select": [ { "name": "urgent" } ] }, "Due": { "date": { "start": "2026-07-01" } } }. Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types.
actions.notion_create_page.description: Creates a new sub-page under an existing Notion page, with a title and optional markdown body.
actions.notion_create_page.props.content: Optional body content for the page. Markdown is supported and converted to Notion blocks.
actions.notion_create_page.props.parent_: The id of the existing page to create the new page under. Resolve via notion_search.
actions.notion_create_page.props.title.d: The title of the new page.
actions.notion_delete_block.description: Deletes (archives) a single block by id, removing it from its page.
actions.notion_delete_block.props.block_: The id of the block to delete. Resolve via notion_get_block_children.
actions.notion_find_database_item.descri: Finds rows in a Notion database matching a raw Notion filter object, returning the first match and all matches.
The id of the database to search. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).

A Notion query filter object. A single condition is { "property": "Email", "email": { "equals": "a@b.com" } }; compound is { "and": [ ...conditions ] } or { "or": [ ...conditions ] }. The condition key MUST match the property's type (e.g. title:{equals}, rich_text:{contains}, select:{equals}, status:{equals}, number:{equals}, checkbox:{equals}, date:{equals}, multi_select:{contains}). Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types.
Maximum number of rows to return (1–100). Defaults to 100.
actions.notion_get_block_children.descri: Reads the body content of a page or block by recursively listing its child blocks, optionally rendered as markdown.
The id of the page or parent block whose content to read. Resolve via notion_search (page) or this action (child block ids).
Recursively retrieve nested children up to this depth. Only used when Markdown is disabled. Defaults to 1.
When enabled, return the content rendered as a markdown string. When disabled, return the raw Notion block JSON tree.
actions.notion_get_database.description: Retrieves a Notion database's schema: its property names, field types, and select/status/relation options.
actions.notion_get_database.props.databa: The id of the database to inspect. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).
actions.notion_get_page.description: Fetches a single page's metadata and property values by id (a database row is a page).
actions.notion_get_page.props.page_id.de: The id of the page (or database row) to retrieve. Resolve via notion_search.
actions.notion_get_page_comments.descrip: Lists all comments on a page, grouped into discussion threads.
actions.notion_get_page_comments.props.p: The id of the page whose comments to list. Resolve via notion_search.
actions.notion_get_user.description: Fetches a single workspace user's details by id.
actions.notion_get_user.props.user_id.de: The id of the workspace user to retrieve. Resolve via notion_list_users.
actions.notion_list_users.description: Lists the people and bots in the workspace, returning each user's id, name, and type.
actions.notion_list_users.props.page_siz: How many users to return per page (1–100). Defaults to 100.
actions.notion_list_users.props.start_cu: Pagination cursor from a previous call's next_cursor to fetch the next page.
actions.notion_move_page.description: Moves a page under a different parent page (or into a database as a row).
actions.notion_move_page.props.new_paren: Move the page into this database as a row. Supply exactly one of New Parent Page ID or New Parent Database ID. The page properties must match the database schema.
Move the page under this page. Supply exactly one of New Parent Page ID or New Parent Database ID.
actions.notion_move_page.props.page_id.d: The id of the page to move. Resolve via notion_search.
actions.notion_query_database.descriptio: Queries a Notion database with the API's native filter and sort JSON objects (compound AND/OR, ranges, dates, contains, etc.).
actions.notion_query_database.props.data: The id of the database to query. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).
actions.notion_query_database.props.filt: Optional. A Notion query filter object. A single condition is { "property": "Status", "status": { "equals": "Done" } }; compound is { "and": [ ...conditions ] } or { "or": [ ...conditions ] }. The condition key MUST match the property's type (e.g. status:{equals}, select:{equals}, number:{greater_than}, date:{on_or_after}, rich_text:{contains}, checkbox:{equals}). Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types. Omit to list all rows.
actions.notion_query_database.props.page: Maximum number of rows to return (1–100). Defaults to 100.
actions.notion_query_database.props.sort: Optional. An array of Notion sort objects. Sort by a property: [{ "property": "Name", "direction": "ascending" }]; sort by a timestamp: [{ "timestamp": "last_edited_time", "direction": "descending" }]. direction is "ascending" or "descending".
actions.notion_query_database.props.star: Optional pagination cursor. Pass the next_cursor returned by a previous call to fetch the next page of results.
actions.notion_restore_database_item.des: Restores an archived Notion database item back to active status by its page id.
actions.notion_restore_database_item.pro: The page id of the archived database row to restore. Resolve it via notion_query_database (with an archived filter) or from the response of notion_archive_database_item.
actions.notion_search.description: Searches the workspace by title for pages and/or databases shared with the integration, with exact or partial matching.
When enabled, only return items whose title exactly equals the query. Disable for partial matching.
Restrict results to pages, databases, or both. Defaults to both (all).
actions.notion_search.props.limit.descri: How many items to return at most (between 1 and 100).
actions.notion_search.props.query.descri: The title text (or part of it) to search for.
actions.notion_update_block.description: Replaces the text content of a single existing block by id.
actions.notion_update_block.props.block_: The id of the block to update. Resolve via notion_get_block_children.
The type of the block being updated — must match the block's actual type (see its type in notion_get_block_children). Defaults to paragraph.
actions.notion_update_block.props.checke: To-do blocks only: tick, untick, or leave the checkbox unchanged.
actions.notion_update_block.props.conten: The new plain-text content for the block. Split automatically at Notion's 2000-char-per-rich-text-object cap.
actions.notion_update_block.props.langua: For code blocks only: the programming language (e.g. javascript, python). Ignored for other block types.
actions.notion_update_database_item.desc: Overwrites property values on an existing Notion database row, identified by its page id, from a raw Notion properties object.
actions.notion_update_database_item.prop: The page id of the database row to update. Resolve it via notion_query_database or notion_find_database_item.

A Notion properties object with the values to set: a map of property name to a typed value object. Only the properties you include are changed; others are left untouched. Example: { "Status": { "status": { "name": "Done" } }, "Estimate": { "number": 5 } }. Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types.
actions.notion_update_database_schema.de: Updates a Notion database's title and/or column schema (add, rename, retype, or remove properties) by id.
actions.notion_update_database_schema.pr: The id of the database whose schema to update. Resolve it via notion_search (filter_type=database).

Optional. A Notion property-schema patch: a map of property name to a type-config object. To ADD or RETYPE a column: { "Priority": { "select": { "options": [ { "name": "High" } ] } } }. To RENAME a column, key by its current name with { "name": "New Name" }. To REMOVE a column, key by its name with the value null (DESTRUCTIVE — drops that column's data). Run notion_get_database first to see current property names and types.
Optional. A new title for the database.
actions.restore_database_item.props.arch: Archived items in the selected database.
actions.restore_database_item.props.data: Only databases shared with your integration are listed.
actions.retrieve_database.description: Get a database's properties, field types and options.
actions.retrieve_database.props.database: Only databases shared with your integration are listed.
actions.update_database_item.description: Change field values on an existing database item.
actions.update_database_item.props.chang: Empty fields keep their current value. Checkboxes are always saved as shown.
actions.update_database_item.props.datab: Only databases shared with your integration are listed.
Items in the selected database, listed by title.
